We're seeing a major regression on the embeddings endpoint since the model-catalog patch rolled at ~02:00 PT this morning. P95 latency jumped from ~110ms to ~850ms and P99 is spiking above 2.2s for our production traffic (see attached CSV with per-minute p95/p99 and sample request IDs). Impact: our similarity search jobs are timing out and our real-time recommendations are degraded. We have a business-critical release dependent on this window.

On Wed, Jun 17, 2026 at 9:25 AM tessa_morgan@redwood.ai wrote:
> Connor / Rishi — forwarding an urgent customer escalation from VoltMetrics.

Thanks for the heads-up. I pulled the traces (thanks Sophie) and correlated them against the catalog deploy timestamps. Preliminary triage: the catalog patch added a new default alias mapping that routes some requests to mixquant-v2 (a quantized variant) for models that previously hit a faster, f16-optimized variant. mixquant-v2 triggers a slower kernel path on certain GPU types — we see a step change in per-token latency in those traces.

Workarounds to propose now:
- Pin the embedding request to model_version=hf-embed-1.2 (previous variant) — this is immediately available and should restore p95 to baseline.
- If customer cannot change requests, we can roll back the catalog alias to the pre-patch mapping (risk: small window of model mismatch for other customers).

I will capture exact trace IDs and link to a short diff of the catalog patch in ENG-2145.

Connor
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for sending the data. We're very sorry for the disruption. Our initial triage shows the issue is caused by a model-alias change in the catalog deploy this morning. We have two immediate options:

1) Quick workaround (recommended): set model_version=hf-embed-1.2 in embedding requests. This pins to the previous variant and should restore latency within minutes. Steps: add model_version param to the embedding API call — sample payload below.

2) If you prefer not to change client code, we can rollback the catalog alias on our side. That will require a short maintenance window while we validate other customers aren’t impacted.

We’ll provide a firm ETA within 30 minutes after we confirm traffic impact. Connor is working on traces and a rollback playbook.

Apologies again — we know you’re on a tight release window and are prioritizing this.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

- Mitigation: Connor recommended either immediate client-side pin or server-side rollback.
- Customer status: Laura has notified VoltMetrics and provided workaround instructions.
- Next steps: Connor to quantify affected traffic and run rollback playbook if >10% traffic impacted. If rollback occurs, we’ll coordinate customer verification and draft a credit plan if SLA breached.

Priyom — marking this for leadership visibility. Happy to hop on a call if needed.
